<!-- pr-reviewer: cd2febfdf92ce5a85f15e4ea93cbf9bd7a0b383c -->
**Ready for the maintainer to merge.** No blockers. This PR changes posted G-code (safety floor), so a second reader read the `haas.cps` diff line by line.

### What looks good
- Each F word of the Haas post goes through `fw()` -> `ff()`. A search of `haas.cps` at the head finds no other `"F"` text. The callers are: linear and compensation engage (l.772), arcs and radius arcs (l.856, l.861), all canned cycles G73/G76/G81/G82/G83/G84/G85/G86/G89 (l.998), and the probe G31 / G91 G1 moves (l.1044, l.1058, l.1075).
- The value does not change magnitude. mm stays `Math.round(v)` and gets a point (`F600.`). Inch stays at two decimals and gets a point when whole (`F2.`). No unit mix and no scale factor.
- NaN and Infinity: `has()` is false, so `fw()` writes no F word, as before. A zero or negative feed writes `F0.` (before: `F0`). This is not a change in meaning. Canned cycles still refuse a feed that is not positive (l.934).
- Words that stay integers did not change: dwell P (ms), S, T, H, D, N, G10 L/P. No X/Y/Z/I/J/K/R/Q formatter changed.
- Goldens: a script check against the merge base. 30 Haas files changed, +658/-658 lines. When the point is removed from `F<digits>.` on the head side, each file is identical to the base. No non-Haas golden changed. No Haas golden (33 files) has an F word without a point.
- The new test `crates/post/tests/haas_feed_decimal_point.rs` is in the lowest crate. Its Gate map names `camcraft_post::post::engine`. It asserts each F word in mm and in inch, requires each of the nine cycles to post, and pins the fraction rule and the refusal. The three updated pins are correct.
- The decision file, the provenance comment (it names the manual section and copies no text) and the line in `assets/posts/AGENTS.md` are present. The PR body is complete: readings, pinning tests, not exercised, `Changelog:`, `Fixes #3681`. No snapshot PNG. No process file.

### Results, merged with main (locally)
Trial merge of the head with `origin/main` 4c0a8dfe3: clean, no conflicts.

| Step | Result |
|---|---|
| `cargo test -p camcraft-post` (whole crate) | 131 binaries, 1068 passed, 0 failed |
| - `haas_feed_decimal_point` | 4 passed |
| app `conformance` | 7 passed |
| app `control_comp` | 5 passed |
| app `fine_bore_cycle` | 9 passed |
| app `program_entry` | 9 passed |
| app `post_cycle_feed_spindle` | 8 passed |
| app `wear_comp` | 5 passed |
| app `posting` | 17 passed |
| app `golden_cl` | 34 passed |
| app `example_catalog` | 39 passed, 4 ignored |
| app `mcp_live` | 14 passed |
| `clippy -p camcraft-post --all-targets -D warnings` | clean |
| `clippy -p camcraft-app --lib -D warnings` | clean |

### Heavy lanes
`cargo xtask gate heavy --base origin/main --dry-run` reaches 24 `app heavy` lanes. This review did not run them. The rule in force for a P1 is one targeted heavy step. The author ran `app heavy: conformance`. That binary has no `#[ignore]`d test, so the step ran 0 tests. It is not a proof of the heavy lanes. The debug `conformance` run (7 passed) compares the Haas goldens. The release gate at the cut is the full check. This is not a blocker.

### Requested before merge
None.

### Notes (not blocking)
1. The feed refusal (`haas.cps` l.136): `msg()` is a warning, and `ff()` still returns `0.`. The engine output therefore holds `F0.` with the warning. The app blocks the post on any warning (`crates/app/src/posting.rs:717`, "post blocked"), so no program is written. The code comment "never written as F0." is true only at that gate. The test `haas_refuses_a_feed_below_its_smallest_inch_step` checks the warning only. The thresholds are: inch below 0.00005 in/min (0.00127 mm/min), mm below 0.0005 mm/min. No real program, dwell-like feed or tap feed comes near them.
2. The fraction rule changes only feeds that round to zero (mm below 0.5 mm/min, inch below 0.005 in/min). A feed of 0.5 to 1.5 mm/min still posts as `F1.`, an error of up to 100 %. This is the precision issue of #3692.
3. G84 tap feed: the PR did not change the rounding, and it did not make it worse. The point removes a factor of 1000 at the default of Setting 77, which is a large improvement. The present rounding error is at most 0.5 mm/min:
   - M3x0.5 at S500: 250 exact, `F250.`, 0 % error.
   - M2x0.4 at S333: 133.2 posts as `F133.`, a 0.15 % lead error.
   - M1.4x0.3 at S115: 34.5 posts as `F35.`, a 1.45 % lead error. Over 10 turns that is about 0.04 mm of axial drift in rigid tapping.
   Follow-up #3692 holds this.
4. `crates/app/tests/fine_bore_cycle.rs:291` has no space after the comma (`"F60."),"{tag}`). `rustfmt` will change it. Cosmetic only.
5. The follow-ups #3690 (other posts) and #3692 (mm feed precision) are named in the PR comment and the decision file.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

Ready for the maintainer to merge.

Trial merge with `origin/main` (`4c0a8dfe3`) is clean. The change is correct and pinned. I found no blocker. One non-blocking note is at the end.

## What looks good

- `ff()` now passes its result through `pt()`, the same helper that the length words use (#1836). The zero literal is `0.`.
- Every feed word goes through `fw()` -> `ff()`: the G1 block, the arc block, the canned-cycle block, and the three probe blocks (`G31` guard/touch, the `G91 G1` retreat). No other code path writes an `F` word.
- Spindle `S`, tool `T`, `H`, `D`, and dwell `P` keep integer words (`ni()`, `"P" + ms`); only the feed changed.
- The goldens change in F words only. I compared each changed `.nc` with the decimal point normalised away: 0 non-F lines differ. 658 additions / 658 deletions, all in Haas files. No bare `F<digits>` remains in any Haas golden.
- The four pinning tests cover mm, inch, a positive feed that rounds to zero (`F0.3`), and the below-step refusal.
- The new test file has a provenance line, a gate map (`camcraft_post::post::engine`), and 244 lines. No new dependency, no process file, no `CHANGELOG.md` edit. Body has `Changelog:` and `Fixes #3681`; the commit subject is conventional.

## Results, merged with `main` (locally, `-j 3`, `RUSTC_WRAPPER=sccache`)

- Build: `camcraft-post` tests and the named `camcraft-app` test binaries compile.
- `camcraft-post` lib: 97 passed, 0 failed.
- `camcraft-post` `haas_feed_decimal_point`: 4 passed.
- `camcraft-post` `comp`: 9 passed; `fine_bore_cycle`: 9 passed; `haas_dwell_cycles`: 4 passed; `recorded_streams`: 12 passed; `script_haas`: 11 passed.
- `camcraft-app` named suites: 97 passed, 0 failed (4 ignored in `example_catalog`). `conformance` 7, `example_catalog` 39, `example_catalog_adaptive` 1, `example_catalog_edge_work` 1, `control_comp` 5, `fine_bore_cycle` 9, `program_entry` 9, `wear_comp` 5, `post_cycle_feed_spindle` 8, `inverted_axis_display` 5, `catalog_groove_part_off` 1, `tool_catalog_fields` 7.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean (54 s).
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean (1 m 44 s).

## Targeted tests

- Decisive mutation: I dropped the decimal for the mm feed path only (`return pt(s);` -> `return inch ? pt(s) : s;`). The pin went RED:

```
mm: F words with no decimal point: ["F51 in `G1 X30. Y30. Z-8. F51`", "F600 in `G1 X60. Y30. Z-8. F600`", "F254 in `G3 X60. Y50.8 Z-8. I0. J10.4 F254`", "F600 in `G1 X30. Y50.8 Z-8. F600`"]
```
  at `crates/post/tests/haas_feed_decimal_point.rs:197`. Then I restored the file byte-for-byte (`cmp` identical, `git diff` empty, md5 `10667de8...`) and the pin went green (4 passed). The pin can fail.
- Example catalog: `example_catalog` 39 passed (4 ignored), `example_catalog_adaptive` 1 passed, `example_catalog_edge_work` 1 passed. `conformance` 7 passed - this is the byte-for-byte compare of the regenerated Haas goldens.
- Light lane (`cargo xtask gate light`): 2 motion twins, both green (`the_slot_keeps_its_verdict_under_sub_micron_perturbations_light` 1 passed in 9 s; `wide_rectangular_pocket_is_cleared_by_parallel_lanes_light` 1 passed in 8 s), exit 0. These are motion tests; the gate runs them regardless of the post change.
- Targeted heavy step (P1): the body names `cargo xtask gate heavy --only "app heavy: conformance"`: ok. That binary has no `#[ignore]`d test, so the step ran 0 tests. The real coverage is the debug `conformance` binary, which compares the regenerated Haas goldens; I ran it (see above).

## Requested before merge

None.

## Questions / notes (not blocking)

1. `assets/posts/haas.cps:136-137` - the below-step positive feed calls `msg(...)` and then still returns `pt(s)` = `F0.`. The in-app post paths block any program that carries a warning (`crates/app/src/posting.rs:717`, `posting_mounts.rs:348`, `posting_per_op.rs:240`), so the app never writes `F0.`. But the dev `post` binary writes `out.program` (`crates/post/src/bin/post.rs:206`) before it handles warnings (`:210`), so a stream with `F 1` in an inch program writes `F0.` on the cutting block and prints a warning. The decision record and the code comment say "never posted as F0.", which holds for the app but not for that dev tool. The pin `haas_refuses_a_feed_below_its_smallest_inch_step` accepts Ok-with-warning and checks the message, not the absence of `F0.` in `out.program`. A later change could make `ff()` refuse the move (as the cycle refusals do), or the wording could name the dev-tool path. This is not a blocker: every in-app post refuses.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
